note: Hand-authored decisions. Consumed by build_manifest.py, which enumerates columns from the live inventory and fails if any column here is missing. A relation-level 'summary' is narrative and never satisfies column coverage.

app_accounts.role: Account root for both manual workspaces and verified Steam accounts. app_users.id and manual_steam_profiles.id are the SAME uuid (readiness 6.1).
app_accounts.summary: Migrated to app.accounts with an integer identity; old uuid retained as public_id. The Steam visibility booleans are PROJECTED to the app.account_capabilities tri-state under the account tuple decision (true->visible; false or NULL->unknown) and the raw tuple is preserved alongside it in app.account_capability_evidence, because the projection is lossy by design.
evidence: docs/v2-m3-capability-decision.md: false is not proof of hidden

id.transform: uuid -> integer identity via migration.account_map, ordered by (created_at, id); the uuid is retained verbatim in app.accounts.public_id so no external reference breaks.
id.note: Identity renumber. The original value survives in public_id, so no fact is lost, but the surrogate key changes, which is a transform not a rename.

account_type.transform: legacy 'manual'|'steam' -> v2 'manual'|'steam'. Value-identical today; carried as transformed because the target is a separately constrained domain (M1:92-93) and the mapping must be asserted rather than assumed.
account_type.note: Also the input to app.steam_profiles.verified: readiness 14.1 flags that a missed mapping silently de-verifies every Steam account.

steam_library_visible.transform: Capability projection, not a value copy: true->'visible'; false->'unknown'; NULL->'unknown'. The raw boolean is ALSO written verbatim to the account-side evidence row, because the projection is deliberately lossy: a legacy false and a legacy NULL both project to 'unknown', so the original flag survives only in app.account_capability_evidence.
steam_library_visible.note: docs/v2-m3-capability-decision.md. lib/steam-owned-games.ts:117 computes libraryVisible as games.length > 0, which cannot distinguish an empty library from a private one, so a legacy false is an availability heuristic and NOT a provider privacy assertion. Projecting it to 'hidden' would manufacture a privacy claim the source never made. 'hidden' remains a legal app.account_capabilities value (M1:146-153) but requires separate validated privacy evidence, which this source does not carry. readiness 8.3 guarded NULL only; the account tuple decision extends the same guard to false.

steam_playtime_visible.transform: Capability projection, not a value copy: true->'visible'; false->'unknown'; NULL->'unknown'. The raw boolean is ALSO written verbatim to the account-side evidence row, because false and NULL are not distinguishable after projection.
steam_playtime_visible.note: docs/v2-m3-capability-decision.md. lib/steam-owned-games.ts:117 computes playtimeVisible as some(hours_played > 0), so a fully visible library in which nothing has been played yields false. That is an availability heuristic, not a privacy assertion, and it must not become 'hidden'.

steam_last_played_visible.transform: Capability projection, not a value copy: true->'visible'; false->'unknown'; NULL->'unknown'. The raw boolean is ALSO written verbatim to the account-side evidence row.
steam_last_played_visible.note: docs/v2-m3-capability-decision.md. lib/steam-owned-games.ts:117 computes lastPlayedVisible as some(last_played_at), so an account whose games simply carry no last-played timestamp yields false. Absent timestamps are not a privacy assertion and must not become 'hidden'.

steam_visibility_checked_at.note: timestamptz to timestamptz, no offset applied (readiness 8.5). The capability decision makes the account-side tuple authoritative as a TUPLE, so its checked time travels with its three flags into the same account-side evidence row rather than being separated from them.

steam_games_seen.note: Last observed owned-library size for the account. app.account_capabilities has no column for it and app.library_sync_state (M1:290) carries sync bookkeeping, not an observed count. Either a new column or an archive; not silently dropped. SETTLED: the capability decision makes the account-side tuple authoritative and names 'games seen' as part of that tuple, so it is preserved with the rest of the raw observation in app.account_capability_evidence rather than dropped for want of a column on app.account_capabilities.

created_at.note: Also the primary sort key for deterministic identity assignment (readiness 6.1).

updated_at.recoverable_from: Row-level mutation bookkeeping with no v2 destination on app.accounts (M1:89-105 has created_at and last_seen_at only). Nothing reads it; it is regenerated by v2 write paths.
updated_at.note: Retired rather than archived: it records when the legacy row was last written, which has no meaning once the legacy row stops being written.

settled_decisions: D-IDN-1 SETTLED: the two manual accounts with no manual_steam_profiles row are reconciled rather than dropped, per plan 14.2 ('do not silently drop two manual account records'). They migrate as manual accounts with no app.steam_profiles row, which app.steam_profiles permits because it is keyed by account. The COUNT must be re-measured at the snapshot, which is snapshot check S-PROFILE-PRESENCE.

app_users.role: Verified Steam identity. Its id is the SAME uuid as the owning app_accounts.id (readiness 6.1), so it is a 1:1 extension, not a separate account.
app_users.summary: Migrated to app.steam_profiles with verified = true. The Steam visibility columns here duplicate app_accounts; precedence is SETTLED by docs/v2-m3-capability-decision.md (the account-side tuple is authoritative as a tuple), and this side is preserved as profile-attributed raw evidence so a disagreement stays auditable. Neither side's false is treated as a privacy assertion.

id.transform: Same uuid as app_accounts.id; resolved through migration.account_map to the integer account id.
id.note: Not a separate identity. readiness 6.1 anchors this to 20260829224140_add_manual_steam_profiles.sql:66 and :128.

steam_id.transform: text (17-digit) -> bigint, with a checked round-trip: bigint value must render back to the exact source text. M1:108 requires steam_id > 0.
steam_id.note: A text-to-bigint narrowing is a real conversion and must be verified per row, not assumed.

display_name.transform: v2 checks length(btrim(display_name)) between 1 and 80 (M1:111-112). Legacy is unbounded and nullable. Whitespace-only normalises to NULL; over-length is a conflict, NOT a truncation.
display_name.note: Nonempty text must not be truncated or dropped (coordinator ruling). Over-length rows are reported, not trimmed.
display_name.conflict: probe P07h counts display names failing the btrim length check

avatar_url.note: v2 bounds length to 2048 (M1:114); probe P07h covers over-length.

updated_at.note: v2 keeps updated_at on steam_profiles (M1:116), unlike app.accounts.

last_login_at.note: The interactive authenticated-login instant is preserved verbatim in the nullable app.accounts.last_login_at timestamptz column. NULL remains NULL if present. It is distinct from app.accounts.last_seen_at, which carries app_accounts.last_visited_at (lib/auth.ts:86); no derivation from visits, max(), or geographic offset is allowed.
evidence: lib/auth.ts:86 distinguishes a long-lived-session visit from a login

steam_library_visible.note: Duplicates app_accounts.steam_library_visible. v2 has exactly one destination (app.account_capabilities). Precedence must be decided from measured disagreement, not assumed. SETTLED: retained as the PROFILE-side row of app.account_capability_evidence, distinguished by source_account_kind and evidence_precedence. It does not feed app.account_capabilities, because the capability decision makes the account-side tuple authoritative; it survives so a disagreement stays auditable instead of being silently erased.

capability_projection.note: Retained as raw evidence only. The mapping is recorded so the profile-side observation can be compared with the account-side one on the SAME semantics during reconciliation; it never writes app.account_capabilities.

steam_playtime_visible.note: Duplicates app_accounts.steam_playtime_visible; same single destination. SETTLED: retained as the PROFILE-side row of app.account_capability_evidence, distinguished by source_account_kind and evidence_precedence. It does not feed app.account_capabilities, because the capability decision makes the account-side tuple authoritative; it survives so a disagreement stays auditable instead of being silently erased.

capability_projection.note: Retained as raw evidence only; recorded on the same semantics as the account side so reconciliation compares like with like. It never writes app.account_capabilities.

steam_last_played_visible.note: Duplicates app_accounts.steam_last_played_visible; same single destination. SETTLED: retained as the PROFILE-side row of app.account_capability_evidence, distinguished by source_account_kind and evidence_precedence. It does not feed app.account_capabilities, because the capability decision makes the account-side tuple authoritative; it survives so a disagreement stays auditable instead of being silently erased.

capability_projection.note: Retained as raw evidence only; recorded on the same semantics as the account side so reconciliation compares like with like. It never writes app.account_capabilities.

steam_visibility_checked_at.note: Duplicates app_accounts.steam_visibility_checked_at. Whichever visibility triple wins must bring its own checked_at, or the tri-state and its timestamp disagree. SETTLED: retained as the PROFILE-side row of app.account_capability_evidence, distinguished by source_account_kind and evidence_precedence. It does not feed app.account_capabilities, because the capability decision makes the account-side tuple authoritative; it survives so a disagreement stays auditable instead of being silently erased.

steam_games_seen.note: Duplicates app_accounts.steam_games_seen, which itself has no destination. SETTLED: retained as the PROFILE-side row of app.account_capability_evidence, distinguished by source_account_kind and evidence_precedence. It does not feed app.account_capabilities, because the capability decision makes the account-side tuple authoritative; it survives so a disagreement stays auditable instead of being silently erased.

settled_decisions: D-IDN-2 SETTLED: precedence is resolved by docs/v2-m3-capability-decision.md. The account-side tuple (three raw flags, checked time, games seen) is the legacy authoritative observation; fields are never selected independently from whichever side is non-null. Differing profile-side evidence is PRESERVED with source attribution in app.account_capability_evidence rather than erased. The 183 disagreements must be re-measured at the snapshot, and a profile-newer, profile-only-dated or equal-time conflicting case is a new exception to reconcile, not permission to flip precedence: that is snapshot check S-VIS-PRECEDENCE.

D-IDN-4 SETTLED: app_users.last_login_at maps verbatim to nullable app.accounts.last_login_at, separately from app.accounts.last_seen_at. NULL stays NULL; no visit-derived, max(), or geographic-offset substitution is permitted. The destination is present in the SQL-derived physical index and is covered by the sibling M3 contract.

manual_steam_profiles.role: Unverified manual workspace built from a public Steam profile URL. id is the SAME uuid as the owning app_accounts.id.
manual_steam_profiles.summary: Migrated to app.steam_profiles with verified = false. This is the other half of the readiness 14.1 verified hazard.
evidence: M1:122-124 unique index on verified steam_id only

id.transform: Same uuid as app_accounts.id, resolved through migration.account_map.

steam_id.transform: text -> bigint with a checked round-trip, as for app_users.steam_id.
steam_id.note: Manual profiles may legitimately share a steam_id with each other and with a verified profile; only verified rows are uniquely constrained (M1:122-124).

display_name.note: User-chosen workspace name. Legacy NOT NULL; v2 nullable with a btrim 1..80 check (M1:111-112). Over-length is a conflict, not a truncation.

steam_display_name.note: Name as Steam reports it, kept separate from the user-chosen display_name (M1:112-113 keeps both).

settled_decisions: D-IDN-5 SETTLED: v2 permits one profile per account because app.steam_profiles.account_id is the primary key, and that constraint is frozen in M1. An account holding BOTH an app_users and a manual_steam_profiles row is therefore a reported conflict, not a schema change. Whether any such account exists is snapshot check S-PROFILE-PRESENCE (probe P03).

sessions.role: Verified Steam and manual-workspace session digests. The source session branch determines app.sessions.session_kind ('verified_steam' or 'manual').
sessions.summary: Migrated to app.sessions; verified rows use session_kind 'verified_steam' and manual_profile_sessions rows use session_kind 'manual'. UUID identity is renumbered to bigint, while the exact decoded digest, account owner, expiry and migration.session_map mapping are preserved.

id.transform: uuid -> bigint identity. Safe because the cookie carries the token, not the id, and no external artefact references a session uuid (readiness 8.7).
id.note: The source session UUID is retained in migration.session_map. A manual_profile_security_intents.source_manual_session_id is an intent-only reference; the intent expires at freeze while the session itself remains migratable.

user_id.note: FK to app.accounts(id) on delete cascade.

token_hash.transform: 64-char lowercase hex text -> bytea via decode(token_hash,'hex'), giving exactly 32 bytes (M1:132). Rows failing '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' cannot be converted and are a hard conflict.
token_hash.note: PRIVATE VALUE. Counted only; never printed, exported to a report, or logged. Legacy has UNIQUE but no format check on this column.
token_hash.conflict: probe P07i counts sessions.token_hash values failing the hex regex; probe P07j counts cross-table digest collisions

last_seen_at.note: Legacy NOT NULL, v2 nullable. Widening, no conflict.

expires_at.note: Subject to the v2 check expires_at > created_at; a legacy row with expires_at <= created_at is a conflict rather than a coercion.

settled_decisions: D-SES-1 SETTLED: plan 14.2 requires the unified session table to decode valid hex digests to 32-byte bytea and to reconcile invalid or colliding digests PRIVATELY. A cross-table collision is therefore a reported conflict with a defined handling, not an undecided design question. Measuring it in the decoded representation across both tables is snapshot check S-SESSION-DIGEST (probe P07j).

manual_profile_sessions.role: Manual-workspace session digests, migrated to app.sessions with session_kind 'manual'.
manual_profile_sessions.summary: Migrated to app.sessions with session_kind 'manual'; UUID identity is renumbered to bigint. The exact decoded token digest, manual account owner, created/last-seen/expiry instants and migration.session_map entry are preserved. Only manual_profile_security_intents expire at the freeze.
evidence: lib/auth.ts:153-196 long-lived manual workspace session reader/writer

id.transform: uuid -> bigint identity for app.sessions.id; the exact source UUID is retained as migration.session_map.legacy_id.
id.note: The browser carries the token, not the source UUID. The map preserves both source and target directions for recovery and deletion.

profile_id.transform: manual_steam_profiles.id uuid -> integer through migration.account_map; the manual owner is retained on the unified session and its session map.
profile_id.note: Foreign keys cascade with the owning app.accounts row.

token_hash.transform: 64-character lowercase hex text -> bytea via decode(token_hash, 'hex'), giving exactly 32 bytes as required by M1:132. A malformed value is a hard conflict.
token_hash.note: PRIVATE VALUE. The exact digest is preserved only in the private target session; it is never printed, exported to a report, or logged.
token_hash.conflict: probe P07i counts manual_profile_sessions.token_hash values failing the hex regex; probe P07j counts cross-table digest collisions

created_at.note: The source creation instant is retained verbatim.

last_seen_at.note: The long-lived manual session visit instant is retained verbatim.

expires_at.note: The manual session expiry is retained verbatim; runtime refresh rules continue to apply after cutover.

settled_decisions: D-SES-2 SETTLED: plan 14.2 and lib/auth.ts treat manual_profile_sessions as long-lived manual workspace sessions; they migrate to app.sessions with session_kind 'manual'. Only the short-lived manual_profile_security_intents are expired and restarted at final maintenance.

manual_profile_security_intents.role: Pending manual-to-verified promotion intents, holding a one-time token digest and the OpenID callback nonce.
manual_profile_security_intents.summary: Not migrated: pending security intents expire at the freeze and the promotion flow restarts. Their value domains can satisfy the v2 branch, and the session FK is no longer a blocker because long-lived manual sessions migrate; the intent itself is intentionally not carried forward.
manual_profile_security_intents.target: not migrated; pending intents are expired and the flow restarts
manual_profile_security_intents.archive_purpose: Prove no pending promotion was silently lost, and give support a way to answer 'my link stopped working' during the cutover window. Counts and outcomes only.
manual_profile_security_intents.archive_retention: Bounded migration staging. Destroyed 30 days after validated cutover (plan 13), correcting the earlier 90-day window. Token and nonce columns are never written to the archive.

retention.account_deletion: Rows carry both source_account_id (uuid) and an integer account_id keyed to app.accounts. Deletion coverage must key on the retained UUID as well as the integer FK, or a row whose account_id is already null survives the account it describes.
retention.account_export: Intent outcome and timestamps only; token_hash and openid_response_nonce are never written to the archive, so neither can be exported.
authority: docs/VaultShuffle_v2_architecture_plan.md section 13: 'Migration staging/exports - encrypted/private; purge within 30 days of validated cutover unless a recovery incident requires retention'
retention.note: The physical archive uses staging-30d-post-cutover, matching the plan 13 bound. This relation contains only cutover evidence; no lasting private fact is retained here.

evidence: lib/auth.ts:330-347 one-time promotion token and nonce flow

id.note: Kept so a support query can identify a specific expired intent without re-deriving it from a token.

source_account_id.note: NOT NULL in legacy, which is exactly what v2's promotion branch requires (readiness 14.8). Resolved through migration.account_map.

source_manual_session_id.recoverable_from: Nothing in the v2 intent domain: the pending security intent expires at freeze. The referenced long-lived manual session is migrated separately to app.sessions and migration.session_map, but no expired intent row recreates this FK.
source_manual_session_id.note: This is an intent-only reference. It retires with manual_profile_security_intents; it does not justify expiring manual_profile_sessions.

token_hash.recoverable_from: Nothing. The intent is expired, so the one-time token authenticates nothing. Excluded from the export and the archive.
token_hash.note: PRIVATE. It DOES satisfy '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' and would decode to the 32 bytes M1:426 requires - readiness 14.8 corrects the earlier claim that it would not - but the intent is not migrated, so that capability is unused.

expires_at.note: Separates intents already dead at freeze from intents the freeze killed.

consumed_at.note: A consumed intent costs nothing at cutover; an unconsumed unexpired one does.

target_account_id.note: Resolved through migration.account_map where the account still exists; null where it does not, which is itself the evidence.

verified_steam_id.note: The Steam identity the intent was about. Needed to explain a failed promotion; it is a public Steam ID, not a credential.

openid_response_nonce.recoverable_from: Nothing. A replay-protection nonce for a callback that will not be completed. readiness 14.8: this is a different, nullable column from token_hash and was wrongly identified as the identifying digest in an earlier draft.
openid_response_nonce.note: PRIVATE-adjacent. Excluded from export and archive.

outcome.note: The terminal state of the intent, which is the whole value of the archive.

settled_decisions: D-SES-3 SETTLED: plan 14.2 and 14.3 expire pending manual promotion intents and restart the flow at final maintenance. The long-lived manual session source is migrated separately; session expiry is not part of this intent decision.

account_merges.role: Audit of manual-to-verified promotions and merges into an existing verified account.
account_merges.summary: Migrated to ops.account_merges, but readiness 4.6 is a real blocker: legacy source_account_id is deliberately NOT a foreign key and the merge path DELETES the source account, while v2 ops.account_merges.source_account_id references app.accounts(id).
evidence: readiness 14 correction: promotions insert (source_id, source_id) and DO satisfy v2's promote branch

id.transform: uuid -> v2 identity; the legacy uuid is retained as a merge tombstone key so a deleted source public id stays resolvable.
id.note: Coordinator ruling: preserve merge tombstones and deleted source public IDs.

source_account_id.note: The readiness 4.6 blocker. Legacy has no FK and the source row is deleted by the merge path; v2 requires a live app.accounts(id). Proposal D-MRG-1 is a 'deleted' tombstone account carrying this uuid as public_id, which satisfies the FK without weakening it and preserves the deleted source public ID the coordinator asked for.
source_account_id.transform: legacy uuid -> integer account id through migration.account_map. A source account deleted by the merge path resolves to a deterministic tombstone app.accounts row with lifecycle_status 'deleted' carrying this uuid as public_id, so the frozen FK holds without being weakened and the deleted source public ID survives. migration.legacy_account_merge_audit.source_tombstone_present records which rows needed one.

target_account_id.note: Legacy already has an ON DELETE RESTRICT FK to app_accounts, so the target always survives.

verified_steam_id.transform: text (17-digit, regex-checked in legacy) -> the v2 column's type, with a checked round-trip if the target is bigint.
verified_steam_id.note: The Steam identity the merge established. Public identifier, not a credential.

merge_mode.note: readiness 14 correction: the promote branch requires source_account_id = target_account_id, and the promotion path inserts (source_id, source_id) at 20260830151421_secure_manual_profiles.sql:352-362, so promotions satisfy it. Only 'merged_existing' is at risk, via D-MRG-1.

analytics_delivered_at.note: Delivery bookkeeping for the legacy analytics sink. M3 keeps this timestamp on the durable ops.account_merges row so a delivered versus undelivered merge remains auditable without a staging-only copy.

account_merges.archive_purpose: Explain a legacy merge whose analytics delivery is ambiguous, and hold the source-account tombstone evidence for D-MRG-1.
account_merges.archive_retention: Durable private fact bounded by the account, not by a feature's lifetime: retained while the account exists, removed with the account, and included in the account export. Coordinator ruling 8 preserves merge tombstones and deleted source public IDs separately, in ops.account_merges.

retention.account_deletion: Archive rows are keyed to app.accounts with ON DELETE CASCADE and carry source/target account UUIDs, so deletion coverage must key on the UUID as well as the integer FK. Coordinator ruling 8 separately requires the merge TOMBSTONE and the deleted source public id to survive in ops.account_merges and app.accounts(lifecycle_status='deleted'); that tombstone is a merge fact, not archived private content, and this archive stores no user text.
retention.account_export: A user's merge history is part of their account export: merge mode, the Steam identity the merge established, and when it happened.
authority: docs/VaultShuffle_v2_architecture_plan.md section 13: 'Account/authored state/retired personal facts - retained while account exists; account deletion removes private derivatives too'
coordinator ruling 12, docs/v2-m3-b-database-batch.md: preserve original facts; do not discard sole authored or provenance evidence
retention.note: Durable because a merge is a lasting fact about the account, not migration bookkeeping. Its bound is the account, not the life of a feature.

settled_decisions: D-MRG-1 SETTLED by coordinator ruling 8: deleted merge source UUIDs get deterministic deleted-account tombstones AND map entries, and the union of existing identities and required tombstones is inventoried before integer IDs are assigned. That is option (a); the frozen FK is not relaxed. Whether any tombstone is actually required must be re-measured at the snapshot: snapshot check S-MRG-TOMBSTONE.

D-MRG-2 SETTLED (manifest-authored, constrained by rulings 8 and 12): ops.account_merges.reason is filled with a constant provenance literal recording that the source predates the field. Ruling 12 says preserve original facts first, and ruling 8 forbids added identity conferring anything it did not have; inventing a user-facing reason would assert a fact the source never held. Subject to coordinator review as an authored disposition.
